chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Takbir in the five Obligatory Salats is ninety-five Takbirs, from which the Takbirs of the Qunut are five.

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرُ: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is Greater), a ritual exclamation.
key_terms.الْقُنُوتِ: Qunut, a supplication recited during the prayer, often in the final rak'ah.

ai.seo_question: How many Takbirs are recited in the five daily obligatory prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi establishes the canonical count of ninety-five Takbirations for the five daily Fard prayers, a metric derived by summing the Takbirs of the opening, ruku', and sujud in each rak'ah alongside the specific Takbirs of Qunut. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential tradition of detailing the precise liturgical structure of prayer, emphasizing the rhythmic sanctification of each movement. The inclusion of Qunut Takbirs highlights the significance of supplication within the formal structure of the obligatory prayer.
